question.problem: Given that the continuous random variable $U$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-\frac{5}{2},\frac{3}{2}],$ compute $P(U\ge 0).$
question.worked_solution:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $U$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

$$
f(u)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{b-a},\, & a\le u\le b, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

Our random variable $U$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-\frac{5}{2},\frac{3}{2}],$ so it has the following probability density function:

$$
f(u)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{4},\, & -\frac{5}{2}\le u\le \frac{3}{2}, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(U\ge 0) & =P(0\le U\le \frac{3}{2}) \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}f(u)\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3/2}\frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{(\frac{3}{2}-0)}{4} \\  & =\frac{3}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
